text:
Maya R: Quick sync — prototyped a small decision-tree compiler that turns Rego-style routing predicates into a compact runtime for SLA/affinity gating. goal: keep policy authoring flexible but make the hot path deterministic and ~O(1) runtime.

Carlos T: curious — what's the p99 impact vs current eval? OPA on the hot path felt heavy in earlier tests.

Maya R: bench so far: pure Rego eval ~1.8ms median, 4.6ms p99 on a 3080; compiled decision tree -> 0.08ms median, 0.6ms p99. big win but tradeoffs: compile step and policy expressivity.

Jun P: what language/runtime for compiled tree? we need something portable across hosted/dedicated/private.

Maya R: output is a small JSON decision table + a C-like interpreter we can embed in Go/Node. also exploring WASM output as an alternative for Private customers.

Lina S: how do we handle irrational policy upgrades? e.g., new rule that redirects 30% of traffic to high-cost region -> need feature flag + metering.

Sam O: +1 on gating. propose rollout plan: (a) author in OPA/Rego, (b) unit test + sim run using historical traffic, (c) compile to decision table, (d) canary with shadow mode, (e) enable with % ramp. also tie to policy-version header so requests carry policy id.

Carlos T: fallback behavior? if compiled policy fails or cache miss, fallback to which allocator?

Maya R: fallback hierarchy: 1) compiled decision table (fast), 2) Rego fallback (slower) for newly authored rules not yet compiled, 3) legacy cost-biased allocator. we need SLA protections: if routing causes >5% p95 latency regressions, auto-rollback.

Jun P: cache invalidation note: policies may refer to tenant metadata (e.g., tenant.tier). if tenant change occurs we must invalidate compiled mapping for that tenant or carry a TTL. leaning toward a versioned tenant-metadata hash included in policy key.

Lina S: telemetry we need: policy_id, compiled_version, route_decision (fast/slow/fallback), decision_path_id, evaluaton_time_us. also a counter for fallbacks and auto-rollbacks. create dashboards per-tenant.

policy-bot: unit-tests: 18 passed, 2 skipped (region-edge rules). see CI: https://ci.internal/repo/1234

Maya R: sample Rego (very small):
```rego
package routing
allow { input.region == "eu"; input.latency < 50 }
allow { input.tier == "enterprise"; input.cost_budget > 100 }
```

Maya R: compiled decision-table example (conceptual):
```json
{"conds":[{"field":"region","eq":"eu","then":{"field":"latency","lt":50,"out":"route-fast-eu"}},{"field":"tier","eq":"enterprise","then":{"out":"route-enterprise"}}],"default":"route-cost"}
```

Sam O: integration note: policy-authoring UI should show a simulated traffic view with expected % changes and cost delta. ops needs an API to force immediate rollback.

Carlos T: perf testing action: Jun + Carlos to run bench on dedicated hardware (A100 v2) and ensure p99 stays <1ms for compiled path under 10k rps.

Jun P: agreed. I'll add load profile + data generator. will also simulate metadata churn to validate invalidation patterns.

Lina S: i'll add telemetry + alerting docs. proposed alerts: fallback-rate > 0.5% sustained over 5m, policy-induced p95 delta > 5% over baseline.

Maya R: next steps: PR for compiler (WIP), design doc for policy-version header + keying, and rollout playbook. I'll open PRs and tag this thread.

Sam O: one more: secret/PII rules — some policies will check customer compliance flags. compiled form must not contain plaintext secrets; ensure policy compiler can reference external secrets at eval time.

Maya R: noted. compiler will emit references to secret ids, runtime will call secure store. no secrets in compiled blob.

Lina S: action items recap:
- Maya: PR for compiler + design doc (policy versioning, secret handling)
- Jun + Carlos: perf + invalidation tests on dedicated GPUs
- Lina: telemetry + alerting dashboards
- Sam: rollout + rollback API spec

Sam O: thanks — this direction feels solid. let's keep OPA for authoring + audits, compiled decision-tree for the hot path. :thumbsup:

Maya R: thanks all. I'll post PR and invite review.
